body_text:
A function $f : A \to B$ with nonempty domain $A$ has a *left
inverse* (retraction) $g : B \to A$ satisfying
$g \circ f = \text{id}_A$ if and only if $f$ is injective. Dually,
$f$ has a *right inverse* (section) $h : B \to A$ satisfying
$f \circ h = \text{id}_B$ if and only if $f$ is surjective; the
assertion that every surjection admits a right inverse is
logically equivalent to the Axiom of Choice. A function possesses
a two-sided inverse if and only if it is bijective, in which case
the inverse is unique.
